name: Authoritarianism
summary: Authoritarianism is rule by a single leader or small group holding ultimate, practically unlimited authority, with the state supreme over other organizations, political pluralism and participation limited, dissenters repressed and individual rights subordinate to the government's needs. Scholars after Linz distinguish it from totalitarianism by its lack of an elaborate guiding ideology, so it says little about economics, religion or social policy.
scope: The ideal type of authoritarian rule as defined in the reference scholarship (Linz's limited pluralism, limited mobilization and mentalities in place of an ideology, as set out in Encyclopedia.com, the Bielefeld InterAmerican Wiki and the ECPS Dictionary of Populism). It excludes totalitarianism, specific regime types (military, party, bureaucratic) taken as separate subjects, and the psychology of right-wing authoritarian followers, which the defining sources do not present as the doctrine itself. Economic, religious, social and foreign-policy statements are left null because the defining sources say regimes differ there.
